page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-16-lssd is an x86_64 architecture server instance featuring 16 dedicated virtual CPUs and 126.0 GB of system memory. This configuration provides approximately 7.88 GB of RAM per vCPU, aligning it with memory-intensive resource profiles. The instance operates on dedicated CPU allocations, ensuring consistent processing performance without resource contention from neighboring tenants.

This server type does not include integrated GPU hardware, making it unsuitable for hardware-accelerated graphics or direct GPU-based machine learning workloads. While the local storage size is designated as None, the underlying storage architecture supports NVMe SSD technology. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4d-highmem-16-lssd offers a high-density memory allocation relative to its core count, providing a balanced profile for workloads requiring substantial memory capacity without the overhead of additional compute cores.

The resource distribution of the Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-16-lssd makes it appropriate for memory-bound applications. Suitable workloads include medium-sized databases, in-memory caching layers, enterprise applications, data buffering, and memory-intensive enterprise workloads that do not require GPU acceleration or large local physical storage volumes.
